items.title: The Duet Behind the Door
items.pitch: Introduce two single adults who keep missing each other's music evenings. A shared life may fill an empty shop with lessons, then leave its last student looking for somewhere else to play.

present_hook.what_you_notice: Two separate home inventories contain complementary duet parts. A vacant shop between the houses never became the lesson room described in an unsigned proposal.

clues.line: {A} attended one evening in {year}; {B} attended the other. Neither signed up for the duet.

window.notes: Require A and B unrelated, mutually compatible adults with verified teaching-level musical skill, distinct homes, voluntary interest in a partner, and no existing partnership that this plot conceals. Bind a lawfully available Main Street music-shop premises and C's genuine later interest in lessons. Present must be at least 30 years later.

interventions.how_it_looks: Bring the two musicians together with the duet parts and let them choose whether to stay.

ripples.headline: Two Music-Evening Regulars Marry
ripples.body: {A} and {B} married after a mutual courtship. The pair chose their own household arrangements.

ripples.headline: Duet Partners Open a Music Shop and Lesson Room
ripples.body: {A} opened a funded music shop employing {B} under agreed terms. Adult learner {C} enrolled in its paid lessons.

effects.to: a permitted accessible home for A and B

ripples.headline: Music Shop Becomes the Teachers' Accessible Home
ripples.body: The retiring teachers closed their shop and completed a funded residential conversion. Continuing learner {C} paid the documented net cost of moving lessons elsewhere.

fails.headline: Duet Introduction Leads to Separate Plans
fails.body: {A} and {B} did not choose a shared courtship in the allotted window. Neither person's existing life was treated as a failed marriage.

present_day.best: In {now}, the former lesson-room window belongs to an accessible home. A residential entrance replaces the music shop's public door; current occupancy follows the residents' actual later lives.
present_day.worst: Failure creates no marriage or jointly inspired shop. The vacant premises may still change through ordinary history.
present_day.twist: The teachers gain a home suited to retirement, while {C} loses a familiar lesson room and pays to continue elsewhere. Their happy ending closes someone else's weekly door.

npc_lines_after.line: I am glad they can stay there. I still miss being allowed to knock and carry my instrument in.

new_rules_needed: Choose one elapsed year per step with a timing key; roll independently using seed, scenario ID, intervention year, role IDs and step. All prerequisites are AND conditions. Check them before rolling. Apply the intervention once. First-roll failure uses fails.chance as its complement, never a separate roll; ineligibility reports the actual reason instead. Stop dependent steps after failure without undoing earlier effects. Resolve concurrent events in stable scenario-ID order with atomic resource and parcel reservations. Recheck survival, age, consent, funds and ownership. Later history remains active. Present descriptions require surviving recorded changes; dialogue requires its stated outcome, a living speaker and actual knowledge.

Marriage requires renewed mutual consent and both currently unmarried, unrelated and eligible. Do not infer an earlier spouse or bereavement; use the conditional alternate title stated in window.notes.

The music store requires the bound premises, priced purchase or lease, inventory, permits and sufficient actual capital; no grant accompanies marriage. B must consent to a real paid job. Add enroll_lessons: record C's voluntary funded lesson enrollment with the qualified provider, without inventing ability.

Add close_scenario_business: close only A's store created in step 2, identified by immutable business ID. Step 3 requires A and B still spouses, actual retirement consent, continuing ownership or lawful purchase of residential rights, funding, residential permission and safe accessible design. convert_use changes that exact premises; it cannot evict other occupants. C must still attend, voluntarily choose a qualified alternative, and have a priced relocation cost equal to the net ten-percent debit; otherwise step 3 is ineligible. Gate C's line on step 3 and memory of the room.
items.era_notes: Use era-appropriate music inventory and accessibility construction. No particular instrument, prior spouse or lifelong teaching career is inferred.
items.why_fun: The same doorway can mean a public welcome in one decade and a private refuge in another. A romance changes an ordinary weekly habit.

items.title: The Lure That Bought the Shore
items.pitch: Invest in a bait shop's tested lure design. A successful license may eventually buy its owner a private boathouse, on the shore where a poorer neighbor used to fish for free.

present_hook.what_you_notice: A bait-shop drawer contains a tested prototype and an unsigned manufacturing offer. Nearby, a privately owned shore parcel still permits free fishing by revocable permission.

clues.line: The offer to {A} expired in {year}. The prototype never reached the proposed production run.

window.notes: shop belongs to A. Bind an actual tested design, lawful licensing rights, a credible unaccepted offer needing development capital, and B's recorded free use of the shore parcel. Require a feasible future purchase and boating use, not public land that can simply be seized. Present must be at least 30 years later.

interventions.how_it_looks: Finance the quoted tooling and testing needed for the bait shop's actual licensing offer.

ripples.headline: Bait Shop Signs a Lure Manufacturing License
ripples.body: The bait shop operated by {A} signed a verified manufacturing license for its developed lure. Payment depended on the actual contract and sales.

effects.site: the bound privately owned fishing shore

ripples.headline: Lure Earnings Help Pay for Shore Purchase
ripples.body: {A} completed a voluntary market purchase of the identified shore parcel. Verified retained earnings paid the documented share of its price.

ripples.headline: Private Boathouse Ends a Neighbor's Free Fishing Access
ripples.body: A permitted private boathouse opened on the purchased shore. {A} lawfully ended the revocable free-fishing permission used by {B}, following an unsuccessful negotiation.

fails.headline: Lure Development Does Not Secure the License
fails.body: The funded development at the bait shop did not produce the proposed licensing agreement. Actual expenses remained expenses rather than imaginary royalties.

present_day.best: In {now}, the identified shore parcel has a private boathouse and restricted access at its former free fishing entrance, if those rights and structures remain in force.
present_day.worst: First-step failure creates no license or shore purchase. Fishing permission can still change through the real owner's ordinary decisions.
present_day.twist: An investment in a fishing business ultimately takes a fishing place away from {B}. The useful invention and the closed gate belong to the same success.

npc_lines_after.line: I bought hooks there for years. The lure did fine; it was my place on the bank that disappeared.

new_rules_needed: Choose one elapsed year per step with a timing key; roll independently using seed, scenario ID, intervention year, role IDs and step. All prerequisites are AND conditions. Check them before rolling. Apply the intervention once. First-roll failure uses fails.chance as its complement, never a separate roll; ineligibility reports the actual reason instead. Stop dependent steps after failure without undoing earlier effects. Resolve concurrent events in stable scenario-ID order with atomic resource and parcel reservations. Recheck survival, age, consent, funds and ownership. Later history remains active. Present descriptions require surviving recorded changes; dialogue requires its stated outcome, a living speaker and actual knowledge.

Add license_design: validate the bound intellectual-property rights and consensual manufacturing contract, debit real development costs and record only actual net royalties as sales occur. Step 2 requires sufficient retained funds, no insolvency or legal prohibition, and a consenting seller; deduct the actual purchase price. No automatic wealth multiplier is awarded.

Add purchase_parcel: transfer the specified existing privately owned parcel, price and encumbrances into A's ownership. Preserve public paths, easements and other people's rights. Step 3 requires A still owning it, a funded permitted boathouse, ecological approval and genuinely revocable permission to B rather than an enforceable access right.

Add revoke_permission: remove only the bound voluntary free bank-fishing permission after required notice. B must still use that permission, and the failed negotiation must occur before the one-time bond decrement. Never close public water or erase a lawful right of passage. Gate B's line on step 3, awareness of the ownership change and actual earlier hook purchases.
items.era_notes: Manufacturing methods and license paperwork follow their decades. A private boathouse requires period-valid permits and never implies ownership of an entire river.
items.why_fun: The player can follow a small invention from a shop drawer to a physical locked gate. Business success acquires an awkward human address.

items.title: The Photograph Nobody Collected
items.pitch: Sabotage a photography studio during its fragile opening year. Its owner may turn a genuine second skill into a shoe-repair business, while an apprentice gives up the portrait work they hoped to learn.

present_hook.what_you_notice: A studio's display shows an uncollected opening-year portrait. A repair-course certificate in the owner's old records hints at another trade that never became a business.

clues.line: {A} opened the studio in {year}. The earlier shoe-repair qualification was still valid, but the portrait trade kept {A.him} busy.

window.notes: shop belongs to A. Require A's independently verified shoe-repair competence, a narrowly viable opening-year studio, a lawful feasible later repair-shop plan and B's real interest in a portrait apprenticeship. No equipment destruction, fire or physical injury is part of the sabotage. Present must be at least 30 years later.

interventions.how_it_looks: Disrupt the studio's opening-year bookings through the game's existing business sabotage action.

ripples.headline: Opening-Year Losses Close the Portrait Studio
ripples.body: The portrait studio operated by {A} closed after its actual opening-year losses made continued trading unviable. Its unsettled bookings followed the real refund process.

ripples.headline: Former Photographer Opens a Shoe-Repair Shop
ripples.body: Using verified repair skills and newly secured capital, {A} opened a shoe-repair shop. {B} accepted a real paid repair apprenticeship rather than the old portrait plan.

ripples.headline: Repair Apprentice Takes Over the Shop
ripples.body: {B} completed a funded voluntary takeover of the repair shop from {A}. The old portrait-training plan was formally abandoned.

fails.headline: Portrait Studio Survives the Disrupted Opening Year
fails.body: The studio operated by {A} remained viable after the recorded disruption. The lost bookings were still real; survival did not refund the harm.

present_day.best: In {now}, a shoe-repair shop occupies its actual leased or purchased premises, with {B} recorded as its successor owner if still operating. The original photography studio is closed.
present_day.worst: If step 1 fails, the studio survives that year's viability check and the scenario repair chain stops. Sabotage still costs the business its actual bookings.
present_day.twist: A useful repair shop can grow from a cruel act without making that act kind. {A} lost a chosen business, and {B}'s paid succession comes with a portrait apprenticeship that never happened.

npc_lines_after.line: I can keep a sole on a boot now. I still wonder whether I would have been any good with a portrait camera.

new_rules_needed: Choose one elapsed year per step with a timing key; roll independently using seed, scenario ID, intervention year, role IDs and step. All prerequisites are AND conditions. Check them before rolling. Apply the intervention once. First-roll failure uses fails.chance as its complement, never a separate roll; ineligibility reports the actual reason instead. Stop dependent steps after failure without undoing earlier effects. Resolve concurrent events in stable scenario-ID order with atomic resource and parcel reservations. Recheck survival, age, consent, funds and ownership. Later history remains active. Present descriptions require surviving recorded changes; dialogue requires its stated outcome, a living speaker and actual knowledge.

Add photography studio and shoe repair shop as business kinds. Apply sabotage through the existing intervention once; step 1 tests resulting actual viability and closes only the bound studio. Failure means survival, not cancellation of the intervention's losses.

Step 2 requires A's skill still adequate, actual tools, permits, premises, capital raised without duplicating compensation, and B at least 18 with voluntary interest in paid repair training. B must independently choose this alternative; poverty does not force consent. Record the paused portrait plan and its real opportunity cost.

Add transfer_business: execute a lawful paid sale or otherwise explicitly funded transfer of the identified repair business, assets and obligations, requiring A's consent and B's completed relevant training and sufficient funds. Add end_training_plan: close only the recorded unstarted portrait apprenticeship, not B's ability to take photographs or study later. No death or inheritance is implied. Gate B's line on step 3 and memory of the earlier portrait ambition.
items.era_notes: Use photography and repair equipment available in each decade. Digital tools may change costs later, but do not erase training or business accounts.
items.why_fun: A storefront changes trades and then owners. The player meets a competent successor whose unrealized ambition is still small enough to talk about.

items.title: The Tunnel Under the Pantry
items.pitch: Have an old cold-storage tunnel inspected before it is sealed. Preserving its harmless echo may eventually draw visitors, while the homeowner upstairs discovers that a local legend can keep very practical business hours.

present_hook.what_you_notice: A house has a bricked pantry stair and a repair invoice describing a voice-like echo. The original inspection request was never completed.

clues.line: The stair was sealed in {year}. Owner {A} called the sound a whisper, but nobody recorded an inspection.

window.notes: A owns the identified house and cold-storage tunnel; B is a distinct resident with no assumed family relation. Bind a genuine safe-to-investigate tunnel, an imminent voluntary sealing decision and a physically plausible acoustic effect. No burial, trapped person or supernatural fact is implied. Present must be at least 30 years later.

interventions.how_it_looks: Offer to pay a qualified inspector, with the homeowner's consent, before the pantry stair is sealed.

ripples.headline: Inspection Keeps the Pantry Tunnel Accessible
ripples.body: An authorized inspection and funded repairs kept the old tunnel accessible. Recorded tests traced its voice-like echo to the actual shape of the passage.

ripples.headline: Old Tunnel Gains a Licensed Listening Tour
ripples.body: Following paid training and site approval, adult guide {B} joined a permitted acoustic tour. Its account described the measured echo without claiming a ghost.

ripples.headline: Tunnel Visitors Gain an Entrance Beside the House
ripples.body: A funded separate entrance opened under the approved access agreement. Homeowner {A} paid the agreed share and surrendered private use of the marked side-yard route.

fails.headline: Inspection Finds No Viable Way to Keep Tunnel Open
fails.body: The commissioned assessment found no affordable approved preservation plan for the tunnel at the home of {A}. Its real findings remained in the records before lawful closure.

present_day.best: In {now}, the preserved tunnel has a separate visitor entrance and a physically modeled echo. The marked access route crosses what was once the house's private side yard, while current tours depend on actual staffing and safety.
present_day.worst: First-step failure leaves an honest inspection report and no invented attraction. The homeowner's later lawful sealing decision follows actual conditions.
present_day.twist: The mystery survives because it becomes understandable and visitable. {A} pays toward the separate entrance and gives up the quiet private side-yard route that made home feel separate from town.

npc_lines_after.line: The whisper never bothered me. The visitors asking whether it whispers on Sundays take more getting used to.

proposed_verbs.does: With A's consent, pay the actual quoted fee directly to a qualified independent inspector for the identified tunnel. Record the report and measurements. Temporarily defer only A's voluntary sealing decision until the report, without overriding mandatory safety closure; buy no favorable findings and create no structural safety.

new_rules_needed: Choose one elapsed year per step with a timing key; roll independently using seed, scenario ID, intervention year, role IDs and step. All prerequisites are AND conditions. Check them before rolling. Apply the intervention once. First-roll failure uses fails.chance as its complement, never a separate roll; ineligibility reports the actual reason instead. Stop dependent steps after failure without undoing earlier effects. Resolve concurrent events in stable scenario-ID order with atomic resource and parcel reservations. Recheck survival, age, consent, funds and ownership. Later history remains active. Present descriptions require surviving recorded changes; dialogue requires its stated outcome, a living speaker and actual knowledge.

Add retain_structure: implement only inspected, permitted and fully funded repairs to the existing tunnel; retain its immutable structure ID. Add record_acoustics: store measured geometry, conditions and reproducible sound behavior. The inspection is paid once by the intervention; first-step funds cover separate actual repairs. No ghosts, invented voices or guaranteed safety are generated.

Step 2 requires the tunnel still safe, lawful public-tour access, insurance, sanitation, trained paid staff and viable demand. qualify records B's completed actual site-guide training, not a universal license. B is at least 21 at the earliest step-2 date. Any house ownership changes must preserve real consent or an enforceable agreement.

Step 3 requires A still owning and occupying the edge-of-town house, B still participating, valid planning approval and construction funding. Add restrict_use: mark only the voluntarily agreed visitor route as nonprivate during specified operating hours while preserving emergency and homeowner access. The ten-percent debit is A's priced net contribution after other funds; refuse the step if resources do not suffice. Construction and access changes are atomic. Gate A's line on step 3, awareness of actual tours and actual Sunday visitor inquiries.
items.era_notes: Use inspection, recording and access arrangements available in each event year. The measured echo may inspire folklore in any decade without becoming evidence of the supernatural.
items.why_fun: The player returns to hear the same strange sound through a different entrance. A harmless local mystery becomes both a destination and somebody's neighbor.
